p4_card.identity: Bumetanide (approved loop diuretic). Identity check 2026-10-27: ChEMBL_37 curates its mechanism as inhibition of the NKCC2 transporter only; NKCC1 appears in three activity rows (two single-concentration inhibition readings in HEK cells and one fitted value in HT-29 cells by rubidium uptake), so the NKCC1 target of the repurposing idea is an activity-table fact, not a curated mechanism.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only IF GABA is depolarising in Wwox-deficient neurons at the relevant age; unmeasured. The CNS penetration of bumetanide is a known limitation (map R-07).
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Map R-07 stands as INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. New: (1) the transcript-level ratio in the one human knockout deposit does not point to a depolarising gradient (descriptive, confounded); (2) the target-identity note above; (3) the single experiment is written out with controls. Neonatal-seizure and autism trials exist (titles retrieved: NEMO open-label dose-finding in newborn hypoxic-ischaemic seizures, PMID 25765333; a phase 3 autism programme, PMID 35292925; a phase 2 autism trial, PMID 32730977); their outcomes were NOT read here.
p4_card.mechanism: Target NKCC1 (SLC12A2); wanted direction: lower intracellular chloride so GABA hyperpolarises; sign depends on an unmeasured quantity.

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried.
directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED is a statement about the record, not about the biology.

Abstract-level statements from PubMed are labelled abstract_only; none carries a receipt.
label_lookup is NOT_ATTEMPTED in the bridge: the bridge has no network. The openFDA adapter was run separately and is recorded in lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md.
No dose, route, schedule or paediatric suitability appears; assay concentrations of the sources are deliberately not reproduced.
